newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FOCUS-Bank of Israel holds key rate steady.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bank of Israel holds key rate steady.

text.p: The Bank of Israel on Monday said it would leave its key lending rate for August unchanged at an annual 12.7 percent after last month's sharp cut of 1.2 percentage points.
The rate is the one charged commercial banks at daily and weekly tenders.
A Bank of Israel spokesman said the decision was made on the basis of recent economic policy and developments on the inflation front.
A change in the foreign exchange rate regime that accompanied last month's rate reduction has led to a depreciation of about four percent in the Israeli shekel.
The government also agreed recently to cut the 1997 budget by 800 million shekels ($226.1 million).
The spokesman said there was a need to monitor the consequences of economic policy in view of the government's 1997 inflation target of 7-10 percent.

June's consumer price index rose by a surprisingly steep 1.1 percent, bringing inflation in the past 12 months to 8.4 percent. But financial markets anticipate inflation will rise to 9.7 percent in the coming 12 months.
Financial markets had anticipated the central bank's decision.
"The market did not expect a change in rates and the decision will not affect trading on Tuesday," said Julien Assous of Sahar Securities.
Analysts said the central bank did not want to appear to be be maintaining a "zigzag policy" by raising rates.
Ilan Shabat, an investment adviser at Israel Discount Bank, called the decision "a wise one" and said the market could use this as an excuse to continue its upward trend, at least for now.
But he warned that the effect of the Israeli currency's depreciation on inflation was uncertain.
"If the dollar continues to rise we may have an interest rate hike in the future," Shabat said.
